$comment: The licences a release may ship, read by scripts/sbom.py; see docs/releasing.md#bills-of-materials-and-the-licence-check. Components are named <ecosystem>:<name>. A first_party entry with a licence gives it to a component that declares none and refuses one that declares another. MartianSecurity/MartianFrontend keeps the same allowed list in its scripts/licence-policy.json.

first_party.reason: The Evals UI's own packages, @martian/evals, @martian/design-system and @martian/client, built in MartianSecurity/MartianFrontend, where each is Apache-2.0 with a LICENSE and NOTICE. The build's ui-version.json names no licence, so this entry records it; NOTICE attributes them.

concluded.reason: The metadata names no BSD variant; the LICENSE file in the distribution is the 3-clause text. The GPL pack files it mentions are test fixtures the distribution does not hold.
The metadata names no BSD variant; licenses/LICENSE.txt in the distribution is the 2-clause text.
The metadata names no BSD variant; licenses/LICENSE in the distribution is the 3-clause text.
The image's CPython interpreter carries no package metadata; its LICENSE.txt is the PSF License Agreement.

exceptions.reason: The Inter typeface in the Evals UI. The SIL Open Font License lets a font be bundled with any software; it is shipped unmodified, with its licence in third-party-licenses.md.

not_checked.reason: The Debian packages of the image's pinned base image, python:3.12-slim. They are separate programs and system libraries that Debian distributes under its own licences, many of them GPL or LGPL; they are listed with the licences their copyright files declare but are not held to the allowed list.
